vocabulary.meaning: 验证；本文为证实某人的看法、给观点背书
examples: But realistically, the term is more likely to validate managers who think that their employees are slackers than to help ordinary workers reclaim their soul.

errors.note: 最开始没认出 validate managers 的语境义，导致人物关系漂移；第7题选 A，正确为 D。

vocabulary.meaning: 懒散的人、混日子的人、摸鱼的人
重新夺回、找回；reclaim their soul = 找回自我
诊断；抽象义为判断、结论
examples: Complex questions such as “Am I running my team effectively?” can be reduced to the confident diagnosis that young people just don’t want to work.

vocabulary.meaning: 说法、主张、断言；不要机械翻成声明
证据、依据；little evidence = 几乎没有；a little evidence = 有一点
examples: The best evidence they had wasn’t evidence at all, but rather a misunderstanding of government data.

vocabulary.meaning: 激增、飙升
examples: Labor productivity is falling after it surged in the first year of the pandemic.

vocabulary.meaning: 倾向、意愿
不愿意、缺乏意愿；dis- 表示否定
卡路里、热量
原指热量高但营养少；本文比喻热闹但实际解释力低
examples: The popularity of these empty-calorie labor trends suggests a divergence between statistical and deeper emotional truth.

vocabulary.meaning: 分歧、背离、分叉
examples: The popularity of these empty-calorie labor trends suggests a divergence between statistical and deeper emotional truth.

vocabulary.meaning: 准……、所谓的、类似但并不完全是
车辆；抽象义为载体、媒介
examples: Put another way, these quasi-trends are bad-vibe vehicles—delivery mechanisms for inexpressible negative ideas about the world that demand the news-headline treatment.

vocabulary.meaning: 难以表达的、难以言表的
难以命名的、难以准确说清的
俏皮大胆的、带点调侃或冒犯意味的
追热点的、追逐潮流的
名词小说；形容词新颖的、新出现的
examples: As a workplace phenomenon, workers’ mild disengagement is about as novel as lunch breaks, and bleary-eyed colleagues stopping by your workstation to mutter.

vocabulary.meaning: 长期的、慢性的；chronic labor issues = 长期存在的劳工问题
examples: Quiet quitting is a bit of novel nonsense that might stand in for chronic labor issues such as the underrepresentation of unions or a profound American pressure to be careerist.

vocabulary.meaning: 代表性不足；under- = 不足，representation = 代表性
事业至上的、过度追求职业晋升的人
新词、新造词、新表达

phrases.meaning: 静默离职；仍在工作，但不再让工作占据全部生活
历史最高点、历史最高水平

examples: The labor force, total jobs, and hours worked increased throughout a period of time when news organizations were telling everybody that work was dead.
The labor force, total jobs, and hours worked increased throughout a period of time when news organizations were telling everybody that work was dead.

phrases.meaning: 数据点；本文为值得观察的事实、证据点
examples: If quiet quitting is fake, the popularity of anti-work neologisms is its own data point that deserves to be taken seriously as a cultural phenomenon.

phrases.meaning: 因 B 责怪 A、把 B 归咎于 A

examples: Complex questions such as “Am I running my team effectively?” can be reduced to the confident diagnosis that young people just don’t want to work.

phrases.meaning: 登上新闻头条、进入公众视野

examples: The term has taken off in part because burned-out or bored workers are simply desperate for a fresh vocabulary to describe their feelings.
When a phrase takes off, it’s often because the new words fill a space of uncertainty, like the coining of a new diagnosis.
Quiet quitting is a bit of novel nonsense that might stand in for chronic labor issues such as the underrepresentation of unions or a profound American pressure to be careerist.

sentences.term: be more likely to A than to B
sentences.meaning: 与其说 B，不如说更可能 A；比较两个可能性
forms: more likely to validate managers who think that their employees are slackers than to help ordinary workers reclaim their soul
examples: But realistically, the term is more likely to validate managers who think that their employees are slackers than to help ordinary workers reclaim their soul.

sentences.meaning: that 从句解释前面名词的具体内容
forms: diagnosis that young people just don’t want to work
examples: Complex questions such as “Am I running my team effectively?” can be reduced to the confident diagnosis that young people just don’t want to work.

sentences.term: not A at all, but rather B
sentences.meaning: 根本不是 A，而其实是 B；强否定加修正
forms: wasn’t evidence at all, but rather a misunderstanding
examples: The best evidence they had wasn’t evidence at all, but rather a misunderstanding of government data.

sentences.meaning: A 并不比 B 少、弱；总结例句不在照片原文中，原文计数为0
即使、尽管 B 正在发生，A 仍然……；常用于两个趋势相反
examples: Earlier this year, several outlets tried to convince Americans that “no one wants to work”, even as the economy added hundreds of thousands of jobs each month.
